about: Editorial suggestions for the Combined edition. Unlike the orthography
checks, every rule here encodes an opinion about how the text should
read, so each one is proposed and never applied on its own.
match:   one entry per consecutive Combined word. Compared on the
consonantal skeleton, so the pointing written here does not
have to agree with the manuscript's.
replace: what each matched word becomes. Leave an entry empty to keep
reason:  shown to the editor, so say why rather than what.
Rules can also be kept in hebrew_phrase_rules.json under the
application data directory; those are read in addition to these.
The five ישו rules that used to live here — one bare and four for the
prefixes ל, ו, ב and כ — moved to hebrew_names.json. A phrase rule has no
prefix peeling, so every prefix needed a rule of its own; the name table
peels, so one entry covers them all. A word the name table speaks about
is skipped here, so a rule an editor keeps for the same spelling does not
give it a second and differently-worded reason.

rules.reason: A title standing in apposition to a name takes the definite article: Yeshua the Messiah.
